name: Haughton Crater (Devon Island)
basis: Cold, dry polar desert with ground ice; analog of Shackleton
source: Lee et al. 2007, LPSC XXXVIII, abstract 2426

name: Concordia Station (Dome C)
basis: Extreme cold and ice of the Antarctic plateau
source: ESA, Concordia: the analogue space mission (2024)

name: Askja Caldera (Iceland)
basis: Volcanic geology; Apollo astronaut training in 1965 and 1967
source: NASA, Apollo program training; Astronaut Monument, Húsavík

name: Atacama Desert (Yungay)
basis: Hyperaridity and nearly lifeless soils, similar to those of Mars
source: Navarro-González, R. et al. 2003, Mars-like soils in the Atacama Desert, Chile, and the dry limit of microbial life, Science 302, 1018-1021

name: McMurdo Dry Valleys (Antarctica)
basis: Hyperarid polar desert: extreme cold and dryness, with water almost only as ice and vapor
source: Marchant, D. R. and Head, J. W. 2007, Antarctic dry valleys: microclimate zonation and implications for Mars, Icarus 192, 187-222

name: Licancabur Volcano and Altiplano lakes (Bolivia and Chile)
basis: High altitude, aridity, a wide temperature range and high UV radiation; high-mountain lakes as an analog of ancient Martian lakes
source: Cabrol, N. A. et al. 2009, The High-Lakes Project, J. Geophys. Res. 114, G00D06

name: Death Valley (Ubehebe Crater)
basis: Arid geomorphology; a site used by NASA since the Viking mission. It is hot and about 50 times wetter than the Atacama core: a partial analogy
source: NPS, Death Valley National Park and NASA host Mars and the Mojave festival; Jones, Bonaccorsi et al. 2013, LPSC XLIV, abstract 2846

name: Río Tinto (Spain)
basis: Acidic chemistry and iron and sulfate minerals, as at Meridiani Planum
source: Fernández-Remolar, D. C. et al. 2005, The Río Tinto Basin, Spain, Earth Planet. Sci. Lett. 240, 149-167

name: Ross Island (Antarctica)
basis: Ice-cemented ground in polar cold: a lunar analog site where drilling and sampling of icy ground were tested in order to look for water ice on the Moon
source: Zacny, K. et al. 2013, LunarVader: development and testing of lunar drill in vacuum chamber and in lunar analog site of Antarctica, J. Aerospace Eng. 26, 74-86, doi:10.1061/(ASCE)AS.1943-5525.0000212
